svg.text: COPPER SIDE, mirrored: what you see when you cut the tracks
18 × 18 holes · cut to 45.7 × 45.7 mm · 10 cuts · 10 links · 2 standoff holes (2.5 mm, for M2.5 nylon standoffs)
Bypass at boot and on any failure: de-energised, IN goes straight to OUT L.
D2 1N4148 — across the coil, band towards +5 V
K1 TQ2-5V — stripe to the top. Pins 1 and 10 are the coil, about 178 Ω
R15 10M — holds the buffer side at 0 V while the relay is in bypass
Connectors (pin 1 is the large filled square)
A1 → IN jack, JST-XH 2-way (B2B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 TIP
A2 → Input buffer, JST-XH 2-way (B2B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 TIP, to the input
A7 → Output L, JST-XH 2-way (B2B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 TIP
A8 → OUT L jack, JST-XH 2-way (B2B-XH-A): 1 GND · 2 TIP
C1 → Control: Pico 2 WH, JST-XH 3-way (B3B-XH-A): 1 COIL − · 2 — · 3 +5 V
No ground: the coil’s low side is switched on the control board, so no
IN gnd reaches the root through A2 only (Input buffer).
OUT gnd reaches the root through A7 only (Output L).
De-energised is bypass. The two NC contacts sit on one strip, so with the
coil off the IN jack’s tip reaches the OUT L jack’s tip and the buffer is
out of circuit. Energised, the jack goes to the input board and OUT L comes
Confirm the contacts with a meter before the audio is wired: pin 4 to pin 2,
and pin 7 to pin 9, should beep with the coil unpowered, and open when 5 V
The IN lane’s ground and the OUT L lane’s ground both pass straight through,
and they are not joined. Neither touches the coil. The coil cable brings no
ground of its own: the transistor that switches it is on the control board.
Unplug this board and the jack cables fit the input and output boards
directly. The pinouts are the same.

Red ✕: cut the track at that hole (red bar: cut between two holes). Lines: wire links on the component side (green carries ground). Strips tinted green carry ground, red a supply, amber 3.3 V. White circles: standoff holes; dashed: what the standoff covers.
